text: {"card_1":{"title":"Where Did the Flood Come From?","text":"How was a flood made? Let's build one in our minds, Kiddo. Egypt is very dry, and it hardly ever rains there. Yet every summer the Nile rose and spread over the fields. Egypt got almost no rain, so where did the water for the Nile's flood come from?","question":"Egypt got almost no rain, so where did the water for the Nile's flood come from?","hints":["Where does a river begin, compared with where it ends?","Rivers flow downhill. It helped farmers grow good crops again.","image_alt":"","read_aloud":"How was the land made fresh again every year? The flood water carried tiny bits picked up on its long trip. Egyptians built their year around the flood, with three seasons: Akhet (flood), Peret (growing) and Shemu (harvest). Officials measured each flood on stone gauges called nilometers. A flood that was too low meant too little watered land. One that was too high could wash away villages.","image_alt":"","read_aloud":"What would you build to measure a river? Egyptian officials measured each flood on stone gauges called nilometers. Too low was a problem, and too high was a problem. The Aswan High Dam, finished in 1970, holds the Nile back in a huge lake called Lake Nasser. Egypt gained steady water for farming all year, and electricity, and no more dangerous floods.
